questions.question:
Given below are some of the measures of the sides and angles of five triangles. Which of the triangles given in the options is NOT congruent to ΔABC?

In ΔABC, m(overline{AB}) = 3.6 cm, m(overline{BC}) = 5 cm, m(overline{CA}) = 4 cm, m(∠B) = 52.4°, m(∠C) = 45.5° 

In ΔDEF, m(overline{DE}) = 4 cm, m(overline{EF}) = 5 cm, m(overline{FD}) = 3.6 cm

In ΔGHI, m(overline{HI}) = 5 cm, m(∠H) = 52.4°, m(∠I) = 45.5° 

In ΔJKL, m(overline{JK}) = 3.6 cm, m(overline{LJ}) = 4 cm, m(∠J) = 52.4° 

In ΔMNO, m(overline{MN}) = 3.6 cm, m(overline{NO}) = 5 cm, m(∠N) = 52.4°
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

A triangle ABC 

AB = 3.6 cm, BC = 5 cm, CA = 4 cm 

angle B = 52.4^circ ,angle C = 45.5^circ

**CONCEPT USED:**

Two triangles are congruent if the corresponding sides are equal and the corresponding angles are equal.

**CALCULATION:**

In triangle ABC,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8891eddd5e325cff0afca7e44eab09672896650fd1ecfe029eb67c2d4ba59e9e.png] 

AB = 3.6 cm

BC = 5 cm 

AC = 4 cm

angle B = 52.4^circ angle C = 45.5 ^circ angle A = 82.5^circ

Now, considering triangle DEF, we have 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/940e8c2b53baef28b359e954604e967240f35d501fd57b30571196ed6c7989c7.png] 

 DE = 4 cm , EF = 5 cm , DF = 3.6cm 

⇒ Since, all the corresponding sides are equal. Hence, triangle DEF is congruent to triangle ABC by SSS ( Side -Side -Side)

Now, considering triangle GHI we have

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d6f404c473f947a4a1c6b76083c78c4d40a2a44c5d530f256a36102cdf42ceb9.png] 

 Now, here we have HI = 5cm , angle H = 52.4^circ , angle I = 45.5^circ 

Since, two angles and one side included between them of triangle GHI is equivalent to the two angles and one side included of the triangle ABC 

Hence, triangle GHI is congruent to triangle ABC by ASA( Angle- Side - Angle)

Now, considering JKL, we have,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/45bc1cbcfd3f20f6fac4934e41607b6aade6e484932b7026980a6ed02d394c02.png] 

Now, here we have JK= 3.6 cm, JL = 4 cm angle J = 52.4^circ Since, angle included between the two sides of triangle JKL is not equal to the angle included between the two sides of triangle ABC Hence, triangle JKL does not follow the property of SAS (Side - Angle - Side ) So, JKL is not congruent to ABC

questions.question:
In the diagram, if overline{AB}||overline {CE}, AG = GD = DH = HB, then which of the following is correct? 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/26c5123fd0cc55b6b588057ad333689dae88b58cce254ca693e886ea1aab98c0.png] 

I. Δ ACG ≅ Δ BEH, II. Δ CDE ≅ Δ DEB, III. Δ HFB ≅ Δ AFG
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In the diagram, overline{AB}||overline{CE}, AG = GD = DH = HB

**Formula used:**

If two lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal.

**Calculation:**

I. Delta ACG cong Delta BEH

Since overline{AB}||overline{CE} and AG = GD = DH = HB, the corresponding angles are equal.

⇒ Delta ACG cong Delta BEH

II. Delta CDE cong Delta DEB

Since overline{AB}||overline{CE} and AG = GD = DH = HB, the corresponding angles are equal.

⇒ Delta CDE cong Delta DEB

III. Delta HFB cong Delta AFG

Since overline{AB}||overline{CE} and AG = GD = DH = HB, the corresponding angles are equal.

But no relation is given about side AF, BF, or angles of the triangle HFB and AFG,

hence, this statement is not right.

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: If ΔABC, DE || AB, where D and E are points on sides AC and BC, respectively. F is a point between C and D such that EF || BD. If AD = 15 cm, DC = 10 cm, then the length of CF is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AD = 15 cm and DC = 10 cm

**Concept used:**

If all the three sides of a triangle are in proportion to the three sides of another triangle, then the two triangles are similar.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b768e4f5c3a8bedb5ee23ee9d46e37e3cad79336d5935b009de93f23091446c.png] 

Let the value of CF be x cm

Now,

In ΔCDE and ΔCAB

⇒ CD/AC = CE/CB = DC/(AD + DC)

⇒ CD/AC = CE/CB = 10/(15 + 10)

⇒ CD/AC = CE/CB = 10/25

⇒ CD/AC = CE/CB = 2/5

Now,

In ΔCFE and ΔCDB

⇒ CF/CD = CE/CB = 2/5

Now,

⇒ x/10 = 2/5

⇒ 5x = 20

⇒ x = (20/5)

⇒ x = 4 cm

⇒ CF = 4 cm

**∴ The length of CF is 4 cm**

questions.question: Two medians DM and EN of ΔDEF intersect each other at G at right angles, If EF = 20 cm and EN = 12 cm, then what is the length of DM?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two medians DM and EN of ΔDEF intersect each other at G at right angles.

EF = 20 cm and EN = 12 cm

**Concept Used:**

Median divides the opposite side into two equal parts.

Centroid is the intersection point of medians which divide the median into the ratio 2 : 1.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ecd01c149ec25c38ddee859555eada4f996abf32ad6c2ec1a55e2657cd478b2d.png] 

In ΔDEF EN is the median.

So, EG : GN = 2 : 1

EN = 12 cm

EG : GN = 8 : 4 

In ΔEGM

EM² = GM² + EG²

⇒ 10² = GM² + 8²

⇒ GM² = 100 - 64

⇒ GM = 6

Since DM is also a median

DG : GM = 2 : 1

DG = 2 × GM = 2 × 6 = 12 cm

DM = DG + GM = 12 + 6 = 18 cm

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: In ΔABC, ∠A = 135°, CA = 5√2 cm and AB = 7 cm. E and F are midpoints of sides AC and AB, respectively. The length of EF (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB (c) = 7 cm, CA (b) = 5√2 cm, BC = a 

E and F are the mid-points of AC & AB.

∠A = 135°

**Concept:**

By cosine rule

Cos A = (b² + c² - a²)/ 2bc

Mid-point theorem

EF = BC/2

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9fc218ac49806bd4bb4f42f9527b6479cf23bb8d94977b36d4aa1fc7edd686a2.png] 

According to the cosine rule

cos135⁰= ((5sqrt2)² + (7)² - (a)²)/(2×7×5sqrt2)

⇒ (-1)/(sqrt2)= ((5sqrt2)² + (7)² - (a)²)/(2×7×5sqrt2)

⇒ -70= 50 + 49 - a² 

⇒ a² = 169

⇒ a = 13, a ≠ - 13

⇒ BC = 13

From formula used

EF = BC/2 = 13/2 cm 

**∴ EF = 6.5 cm**

questions.question: ABC is a right-angled triangle, right-angled at B. D is a point on AC such that AD = 12 cm and CD = 16 cm. If BD bisects ∠ABC , then the perimeter of ΔABC will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AD = 12 cm and CD = 16 cm

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50b6807e9e4d1d2ef685dc9e0ced84523b4d15588b2111ef209e0ce17a9ee64d.png] **

BD is angle bisector of ∠ABC.

⇒ AD/CD = AB/BC

⇒ AB/BC = 12/16 = 3/4

Let AB and BC be 3a and 4a respectively.

Using pythagoras theorem,

⇒ AC² = AB² + BC²

⇒ AC = 5a

⇒ AD + DC = AC

⇒ AC = 12 + 16 = 28

⇒ 28 = 5a

⇒ a = 5.6

**∴ Perimeter of ΔABC = 3a + 4a + 5a = 12a = 67.2 cm**

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, AP the bisector of ∠A, is perpendicular to BC at point P The measures of BP and PC are x and 3y, respectively: The measures of AB and AC are 4x and (5y + 21), what is the value of (x + y)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠BAP = ∠CAP

BP = x ; PC = 3y

AB = 4x ; AC = (5y + 21)

**Concept used:**

Angle bisector bisects the third side into their two corresponding side ratio.

**Calculation: ** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f817002fa8b5122a6342275a94f44c8b66c9c9fc19878814cfcd35034047a246.png] 

⇒ BP/PC = AB/AC

⇒ x/3y = 4x/(5y + 21)

⇒ 5y + 21 = 12y

⇒ 7y = 21

⇒ y = 3

Now,

In △ APB & △ APC

AP = AP (Common)

∠P = ∠P = 90° 

∠BAP = ∠CAP

∴ △ APB ≅ △ APC (By ASA)

By C.P.C.T

x = 3y

⇒ x = 3 × 3 = 9

Now, x + y = 9 + 3 = 12

**∴ The value of (x + y) is 12.**

questions.question: BD and CE are the medians of Δ ABC, right angled at A. If CE = frac{{5sqrt {13} }}{2} cm, BC = 10 cm, then the length of BD is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

BD and CE are the medians of Δ ABC

CE = 5√13/2 cm

BC = 10 cm

**Concept used:**

When two median is given, then add the two numbers in the middle and then divide by 2.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/edb53fbe5497401ebeeb640a1c2227121465f95e52c4973a866eeaa6287c0cff.png] 

According to the question

⇒ BD² = AB² + (AC/2)²

⇒ BD² = AB² + AC²/4

Now,

CE² = (AB/2)² + AC²

⇒ AB²/4 + AC²

Now,

BD² + CE² = 5/4(AB² + AC²)

⇒ BD² + CE² = 5/4 BC²

⇒ BD² + (5√13/2)² = 5/4 × (10)²

⇒ BD² + 325/4 = 5/4 × 100

⇒ BD² + 325/4 = 125

⇒ BD² = (125 – 325/4)

⇒ BD² = (500 – 325)/4

⇒ BD² = 175/4

⇒ BD = 5√7/2 cm

**∴ The length of the BD is 5√7/2 cm**

questions.question: The sides ST and TR and the median SU of the Δ STR are equal to the sides MN and NJ and the median MV of the Δ MNJ, respectively. If ∠TSU = 46°, ∠NMJ = 79°and ∠MVN = 88°, what is the degree measure of = (7)/(11)∠SRT?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since U and V are midpoints of TR and NJ, TR = NJ ⇒ TU = NV.

By SSS congruence, ΔSTU ≅ ΔMNV (ST = MN, SU = MV, TU = NV).

This gives ∠NMV = ∠TSU = 46° and ∠MNJ = 180° − (46° + 88°) = 46°.

In ΔMNJ, ∠MJN = 180° − (∠MNJ + ∠NMJ) = 180° − (46° + 79°) = 55°.

By SAS congruence, ΔSTR ≅ ΔMNJ ⇒ ∠SRT = ∠MJN = 55°.

Required measure = 7/11 × 55° = 35°.

**∴ The correct answer is 35°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Sides ST = MN

⇒ Side TR = NJ

⇒ Median SU = Median MV

⇒ ∠TSU = 46°, ∠NMJ = 79°, and ∠MVN = 88°

**Formula Used:**

⇒ SSS Congruence Rule: If three sides are equal, the triangles are congruent.

⇒ SAS Congruence Rule: If two sides and the included angle are equal, the triangles are congruent.

 
 
• S T R U 46° 
 
• M N J V 79° 88° 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• ∴ ∠SRT = 55° 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since SU and MV are medians, U and V divide the bases TR and NJ into equal halves.

⇒ TR = NJ ⇒ TR/2 = NJ/2 ⇒ TU = NV

⇒ Consider ΔSTU and ΔMNV: ST = MN, SU = MV, and TU = NV.

⇒ By SSS congruence, ΔSTU ≅ ΔMNV.

⇒ This implies corresponding angles are equal: ∠NMV = ∠TSU = 46°, and ∠SUT = ∠MVN = 88°.

⇒ In ΔMNV, using angle sum property: ∠MNV = 180° − (46° + 88°) = 46°.

⇒ Angle ∠MNJ is the same as ∠MNV, hence ∠MNJ = 46°.

⇒ In the full ΔMNJ, angle sum property gives: ∠MJN = 180° − (∠MNJ + ∠NMJ) = 180° − (46° + 79°) = 55°.

⇒ Now compare ΔSTR and ΔMNJ: ST = MN, TR = NJ, and the included angles ∠STR = ∠MNJ (since ΔSTU ≅ ΔMNV).

⇒ By SAS congruence, ΔSTR ≅ ΔMNJ.

⇒ Therefore, corresponding angles are equal: ∠SRT = ∠MJN = 55°.

⇒ Required value = 7/11 × ∠SRT = 7/11 × 55° = 35°.

**∴ The correct answer is 35°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Congruence of Triangles (SSS and SAS)

Two triangles are identically congruent if all three corresponding sides are equal (SSS), or if two sides and the included angle are equal (SAS). Congruent triangles have exactly the same size and shape.

Median of a Triangle

A line segment joining a vertex to the exact midpoint of the opposite side. It cleanly divides the opposite side into two identical half-segments.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles in any planar triangle always equals 180°. This is a fundamental rule used repeatedly to find unknown missing angles.
